single large animal occupying the broad face of an upright pillar

justification: Both surfaces show a single quadruped in strict profile rendered in shallow raised relief on the broad face of a tall upright pillar, in each case with legs bent and a long tail sweeping up and over the back — a fairly specific and conventional scheme rather than a generic 'some animal'. The main difference is scale and clarity of the figure relative to its field: in B the beast dominates the whole face with an exaggerated, elongated arching tail and clearly modelled head and paws, while in A the creature is small, more compact and set among other faint carved details on the shaft, so posture and proportions are not exactly matched.
